question: The parts of a screen that change as a person uses it are called:
option_a: State

question: The parts of a screen that stay the same no matter what the person does are called:
option_a: Layout

question: A named box that holds one piece of information that can change is a:
option_a: Variable

question: A designer built four nearly identical screens that differ only by the number in the cart. The real problem is:
option_a: The number is state and should be a variable, not four frames
option_b: The screens are not aligned to each other
option_c: There are too few screens for a real app
option_d: The cart icon is in the wrong corner

question: A variable that holds only true or false is which type?
option_a: Boolean

question: A variable that counts how many items are in a cart should be which type?
option_a: Number

question: A variable that stores which tab is selected, from a small set of names, is best as which type?
option_a: String

question: Why is a boolean better than the text 'yes' for storing whether an item is favorited?
option_a: There are only two possible answers, and text introduces variations like Yes, YES, and yes that will not match
option_c: Text cannot be used in prototypes

question: By convention, a boolean variable's name usually starts with:
option_a: is or has

question: A variable's starting value is important because it determines:
option_a: What the person sees the very first time, which is the empty state
option_c: Which frame the prototype opens on

question: In a prototype, clicking the Add button does not change the count. The most likely cause is:
option_a: The interaction is attached to the wrong layer
option_b: The variable was given the wrong name
option_c: The file has not been published

question: A counter goes from 0 to 1 and then never changes again. The most likely cause is:
option_a: The action sets the variable to a fixed value instead of the variable plus one
option_b: The variable is a string instead of a number
option_c: The button is hidden behind another layer
option_d: The prototype is set to Instant

question: Making a text layer display a variable's current value is called:
option_a: Binding it to the variable

question: The main reason one frame that changes is better than four frames that do not is:
option_a: Every future edit only has to be made once, so the screens cannot fall out of sync
option_b: One frame uses less disk space
option_c: Four frames is against Figma's rules
option_d: Prototypes can only have one frame

question: With variables, an empty state stops being a separate screen you drew and becomes:
option_a: A condition, checked against the current value

question: A designer wants a cart badge to appear only when the cart is not empty. The right tool is:
option_a: A conditional that checks whether the count is greater than zero
option_b: A second frame with the badge drawn on it
option_c: A thicker border on the badge

question: UX refers to:
option_a: The overall experience of using a product
option_b: Only the colors and fonts on screen

question: UI refers to:
option_a: The specific screens and controls a person interacts with
option_b: How long a product takes to build
option_c: The target market for a product

question: A low-detail sketch showing where things go, without final colors or images, is a:
option_a: Wireframe

question: A clickable version of a design that a person can actually move through is a:
option_a: Prototype

question: How many primary actions should a single screen have?
option_a: One

question: Which is NOT a reliable way to make a primary action stand out?
option_a: Making it the only element in a serif typeface
option_b: Giving it more contrast than anything else
option_c: Giving it more size than anything else

question: Breaking a well-known interface convention costs you because:
option_a: People have to stop and think about something they already knew how to do

question: During a user test, every time the designer wants to explain something, it means:
option_a: That part of the interface is not explaining itself
option_b: The tester is not paying attention
option_d: The explanation should be added to the screen as text

question: The screen a person sees before they have added any content is the:
option_a: Empty state

question: A window that appears on top of the current screen and must be dealt with before continuing is a:
option_a: Modal

question: In most mobile apps, the back control belongs:
option_a: In the same corner on every screen
option_b: Wherever there is room on each screen

question: A reusable element you can place many times and update from one place is a:
option_a: Component

question: The strongest reason to sketch on paper before building in Figma is:
option_a: It settles the structure before time is spent on color and detail
option_b: Paper is cheaper than a computer

question: A project's scope is too large when:
option_a: There is no way to finish one complete task end to end in the time available
option_b: It has more than three screens
option_c: It uses more than two colors

question: A typeface with small strokes on the ends of its letters is:
option_a: Serif

question: The squint test checks:
option_a: Whether the most important thing still stands out when detail disappears
option_d: Whether the text is spelled right

question: Grouping related items close together and unrelated items further apart is the principle of:
option_a: Proximity

question: If every element on a screen is the same size and weight, the result is:
option_a: No hierarchy, so nothing is emphasized

question: To submit a flat version of a design that anyone can open, export as a:
option_a: PDF

question: You need to show a prototype on a portfolio page so visitors can click through it. The right approach is:
option_a: Embed the live prototype and confirm it works on the published page
option_c: Export a single PDF of the home screen
option_d: Paste a link to your edit URL
